newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse fall may start next week - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse fall may start next week - analysts.

text.p: Polish shares eased this week and analysts said they might start out flat next week before a deeper correction hit, erasing a significant part of the bourse's 38-percent growth since mid-December.
Some analysts said that though a fall was soon likely, the market was still strong enough to rise to new 35-month highs next week before the profit-taking correction ensued.

"The market is overheated, the number of orders is up and stocks are expensive, so a correction is imminent, but I think the market has enough momentum to rise to new highs and only later fall," said Piotr Leszczuk of Bank Slaski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.2 percent this week to 18,136.2 points, dipping after having set a 35-week high on Tuesday at 18,339.4 points.
Analysts said a correction could pull the main WIG index down to 16,000 or 15,000 points after a month or so.
They said the food-price figure for February 11-20 expected next Friday was unlikely to move the market, which does not expect a change in official interest rates in the next two to three months.

Some analysts said banks, which make up about 40 percent of market capitalisation, seemed overvalued with their sector price-earnings ratio of 10.4 times historic earnings, and could be significantly hit by the expected correction.

But they said the construction sector's prospects and earnings forecasts for 1997 were very good and that even the sector's p/e ratio of 54.4 did not make their shares less attractive in the face of an expected Polish construction boom.
Analysts said public offerings next week were not large enough to draw much capital from the secondary market and should not influence prices on the exchange.
On Monday Jelfa's 500,000-share retail offering opens, as does the first subscription period of Mostostal Export's 1-for-50 rights issue.

On Tuesday pipe maker Ferrum starts its initial public offering, including a large-investor 2.4-million-share tranche, and trader BEST on Friday ends the 300,000-share small-investor tranche of its public offering.
The week's top gainers were Kable, which jumped 21.7 percent on good January earnings reported on Tuesday, and Relpol, which rose 18.8 percent.
The biggest losers were Bank Gdanski, which fell 10.5 percent and Jelfa, which fell 10.2 percent after announcing a new-issue price lower than its market price, traders said.
